messages:
Maria: Heads-up — customers on canary report higher tail latency after the v12.6 runtime roll. Noticed p95 up ~120ms and p99 up ~350ms on hosted/generate. Started 2026-03-15T02:34:27Z.
Ashok: Saw same on dashboards. Canary is at 5% traffic. Baseline v12.5 numbers were stable. This looks isolated to GPU pool gpu-pool-5 and quantized routes.
DeployBot: Deploy v12.6 canary rolled to 5% at 2071234400 by ashok. Release notes: adaptive-kernel-ranking + kv-alignment-fix + mempool tweak.
Kai: Do we have model or seq-length correlation? Any spikes on embeddings endpoints?
Maria: Embeddings unaffected. Generation routes most impacted: gpt-medium-16k-quant and gpt-legacy-4k. Short prompts okay; long-prefix requests show worst tails.
Sam: Pulled runtime logs from affected instances, seeing frequent kernel fallback events and increased memcpy times. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T02:35:02Z] kernel_ranker: scored candidates [v2,v1,v3] -> chosen v2 (score 0.82)
[2026-03-15T02:35:02Z] kernel_exec: memcpy_ms=42 exec_ms=210
[2026-03-15T02:35:03Z] fallback: kernel_v1 used after v2 stall
```
Nina: Interesting. v2 should be faster for long sequences but maybe suffers with our allocator pattern. Any mempool warnings?
Sam: Yes, occasional mempool fragmentation messages before fallback.
Ashok: Immediate customer-facing mitigation options: 1) reduce canary to 0% 2) route quantized models to v12.5 only 3) enable a temporary per-model override to prefer kernel_v1.
Maria: I prefer a surgical approach — route just the affected models off v12.6 while keeping the rest of canary for rollout telemetry.
DeployBot: Applying route rule: split canary so gpt-medium-16k-quant + gpt-legacy-4k go to v12.5, others remain on v12.6 (requested by maria)
DeployBot: Route update applied at 2071234520.
Maria: Post-route metrics: p95/p99 for affected customers return to baseline within ~90s. Canary traffic overall stable.
Kai: Next step: bisect the adaptive-kernel-ranking changes. There are 8 commits touching ranker and 3 touching mempool. I propose narrowing to ranker commits first.
Sam: Bisect plan proposal:
- Build v12.6 variants with feature flag KERNEL_RANKER=old/new at binary level.
- Run synthetic traffic job that mirrors our long-prefix distribution (seq lengths 2k-14k, 70% long tails).
- Compare p95/p99 and kernel fallback rates.
Commands we used to push test builds:
```
make runtime-image VERSION=12.6-bisect-ff
docker tag runtime:12.6-bisect-ff registry/redwood/runtime:12.6-bisect-ff
deploy --service=runtime --version=12.6-bisect-ff --env KERNEL_RANKER=legacy --route=canary --instances=1
```
Nina: I'll add perf counters to the ranker logs (latency_ns, chosen_candidate, allocator_free_bytes) and ship to s3/telemetry so we can compare decisions across builds.
Ashok: Also let's enable tracing on a single canary instance with pprof to capture memcpy hotspots.
Sam: Ran the legacy-ranker build on one instance and replayed the synthetic workload. Observed p99 drop from ~480ms to ~170ms on that instance; fallback events dropped 8x.
Kai: That strongly implicates ranker changes. Suggest binary search across the 8 ranker commits to find the exact commit introducing regression.
Maria: Who can run the bisect? Sam + Kai please. Ashok will coordinate rollbacks if we need to widen routing.
Sam: I'll own the bisect infra. Plan: automate creating 3 intermediate builds each round, run 10k simulated requests, collect p95/p99 and kernel fallback rates, and stop after identifying the bad commit.
Kai: I'll own the ranker log instrumentation and analysis script to match inputs -> chosen kernel.
SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-02 severity: medium. Impact: canary customers on quantized routes. Mitigation: route affected models to v12.5. Ticket: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0315-02
Ashok: Customer comms: support informed affected customers and offered to move their traffic off canary; no SLA credits required yet but offer on request.
Maria: Post-bisect fixes: if a single commit is guilty we should either revert it or patch ranker to include allocator-aware penalty. If multiple commits interact, may need fallback to conservative scoring until mempool fixes land.
Nina: Also add a short-term automated circuit: if kernel fallback rate > 1% for a model for 2 minutes, route that model to legacy kernel automatically.
Sam: I'll prototype the circuit and add it to the canary routing controller. Should be low-risk and buys us time.
Maria: Good. Timeline: bisect + fix + canary re-roll targeted within 36 hours. I'll update the incident page with all artifacts. Thanks everyone.
Kai: Adding a note: add perf regression guard to PR checks for ranker — run the synthetic harness and require no >20% p99 delta.
Sam: On it.
Ashok: Closing operational loop — will keep canary scoped and escalate if customers report anything after today's changes.
Maria: Closing thread for now. Will reopen with bisect results and artifacts. :rocket:
